claims.text: Increasing nanoscale chemical short-range order enhances local magnetoelastic coupling.
Enhanced local magnetoelastic coupling sharpens the magnetization change under low applied fields.
Increasing short-range order reduces magnetic hysteresis.
Coherent nanostructured short-range-order interfaces favor rapid phonon-mediated heat exchange.
The proposed short-range-order nanostructure maintains mechanical stability.
Equiatomic FeCoNiTi is a rare-earth-free alloy composition.
The initial FeCoNiTi material can be prepared as an as-cast, rapidly quenched polycrystalline alloy.
Rapid quenching gives the as-cast alloy a relatively low degree of chemical short-range order.
The as-cast FeCoNiTi-type baseline has a moderate magnetocaloric response.
Controlled low-temperature annealing promotes the formation and percolation of chemical short-range-order clusters.
A suitable annealing treatment can increase short-range order without causing deleterious secondary phases or grain coarsening.
Annealing at 300–500 K is below a magnetic ordering temperature of equiatomic FeCoNiTi.
Applied fields of 1 T or less constitute an operating regime relevant to magnetic refrigeration for this alloy.
Annealing produces nanometer-scale chemically ordered clusters with coherent interfaces.
Enhanced short-range order allows a small external field to induce a more abrupt and reversible magnetization change.
Coherent short-range-order interfaces provide low-thermal-resistance pathways for phonon transport.
Short-range-order interfaces impede dislocation motion and thereby preserve mechanical stability.
Relative to the quenched baseline, the annealed alloy will have larger low-field adiabatic temperature and isothermal magnetic entropy changes.
Relative to the quenched baseline, the annealed alloy will have narrower magnetic hysteresis loops.
Relative to the quenched baseline, annealing will leave yield strength and ductility unchanged or improve them.
